messages:
Maria Chen: Posted two small mocks for the Account form. Variant X = dense inline errors (short lines under fields). Variant Y = micro-markers + top expandable banner on submit. Also sketched 3 delete flows (undo snackbar, confirm-by-name, typed phrase). Need quick takes on mobile density and a11y. Devin Patel: Quick read: Variant X is very discoverable for single-field fixes. Variant Y better for long multi-section saves. Mobile concern: expandable banner can be missed when keyboard is open. Samir K.: For tables, inline copy will crowd. Suggest hybrid: tiny inline indicators + banner that expands when errors > 2. Also prefer explicit "Required" text for critical inputs (not only *). Rika Sato: A11y note: banner must be in an assertive live region and we should move focus into it on failure. Example: ```
Could not save 4 fields need attention.
``` Rika Sato: Also ensure aria-invalid and aria-describedby tie fields to messages. Don't rely on color alone. Maria Chen: Copy suggestion for banner: "Could not save 4 fields need attention. Expand for details or fix inline." Keep tone direct. Devin Patel: For required markers: asterisk + visible "Required" for desktop. On narrow screens hide the word but keep aria-required. Samir K.: Delete confirmations: my rule: undo snackbar for soft/bulk clears, exact-name for org-level deletes, typed-phrase for irreversible cross-account wipes. Consider a short cooldown for bulk repeat deletes. Rika Sato: Accessibility for typed-phrase: make the input tabbable, announce pattern, and provide clear instructions. Ensure contrast for helper text >=4.5:1 (current mock was 3.2:1). DesignBot: Scan results: inline helper contrast 3.2:1 (fail). Banner missing programmatic focus on submit fail. Recommend aria-label="Form errors" and focus move + `aria-invalid` on invalid inputs. Maria Chen: Action items: 1) boost helper contrast or use bolder weight, 2) add assertive banner + focus transfer, 3) implement explicit "Required" text on dense forms, 4) codify confirmation rules (undo vs exact-name vs typed-phrase). I'll post updated mocks later. Tagging @Samir to draft exact-name wording. :nerd_face:
